newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ minor parties' chances improve - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: NZ minor parties' chances improve - newspaper.

text.p: The Christian Coalition and ACT New Zealand could double their support if opinion polls continue to show they are likely to win seats in Parliament, according to research commissioned by the Sunday Star-Times.

More than 40 percent of voters surveyed said they would consider voting for a minor party now that there were signs that at least the Christians and ACT would break the MMP vote threshold and get sets in parliament, the paper said on Sunday.

"Labour stands to be the biggest casualty if this voter switch takes place," the paper said. More than half of current Labour supporters said they would consider switching to vote for a smaller party if one looked like succeeding.
Research of the latest TV3-CM Research Gallup poll showed there was a significant potential voting bloc for the two minor parties.
So far, 29 percent of all voters have not planned to vote for any small party for fear of their vote being wasted, should the party fail to break the five percent threshold.
A further 29 percent said they were simply not interested in the smaller parties' policies.
However, poll responses suggested strongly that voter attitudes would change significantly if it became clear a small party had enough support to break the threshold.
The Christian Coalition has broken through five percent in at last two recent polls and ACT is hovering over four percent.
The poll, taken from August 29 to September 1, found the potential vote for the Christians was nine percent and eight percent for ACT.

Depending on how much the two parties eat into National's support base, their success could mean the difference between National staying in the Beehive or leading the Opposition after the October 12 election, the paper said.
